The failing ALLOCATE object first goes through `gfc_resolve_expr (e)` at the top of `resolve_allocate_expr`, so this function is on the direct execution path. If the expression for a function-result component is routed or normalized incorrectly here, later ALLOCATE-object checks will see the wrong expr_type or metadata.

Relevant because the second diagnostic is explicitly about variable-ness, and this function resolves EXPR_VARIABLE references, applies `gfc_variable_attr (e, &e->ts)`, resolves refs, and handles various special cases for associated/class/coindexed variables. It is slightly less likely than the EXPR_FUNCTION-aware routines because the problematic construct is a function result component, but if that expression is being converted into or mishandled as a variable reference during resolution, this method is a likely contributor.
